brief: NVIDIA's FQ3 revenue of $115.8B beat UBS and Street estimates by 5-6%, with Data Center about 5% ahead and Edge Compute about 14% ahead; gross margin of 74.9% and EPS of $2.68 also beat. FQ4 guidance of about $130B revenue and 71-72% gross margin matched UBS's preview, and NVIDIA raised C2027 revenue growth guidance from 70% to 75%, which UBS reads as strong conviction in 2027 demand backed by over $100B of added C2027 supply commitments. But supply commitments for C2028 and C2029 rose only slightly, so UBS's standing worry shifts from C2027 cuts to how much growth decelerates in C2028, with a related risk that NVIDIA becomes beholden to its own purchase commitments to keep funding customer revenue. Talent retention after recent management changes, plus a 10-Q delay tied to an ongoing investigation, add governance uncertainty. Management told UBS that Southeast Asia licensing rules are not denting customer plans. UBS trims its price target to $220 from $240, unchanged 12x C2028E multiple on a lowered $18.80 EPS estimate, and keeps its Buy rating.
